title: Fit-to-Fly Medical Clearance After Plastic Surgery in Türkiye
seoTitle: Fit-to-Fly Clearance After Plastic Surgery in Türkiye (2026)
metaDescription: Understand fit-to-fly timelines after surgery in Türkiye, DVT cabin risks, IST wheelchair and lounge booking, and how to handle extended stays.
quickAnswer: Most plastic surgeons clear short-haul flights 5 to 14 days after surgery depending on procedure scope, while long-haul flights over four hours require stricter blood-clot evaluation. Always obtain a signed fit-to-fly letter, reserve Istanbul Airport wheelchair assistance 48 hours ahead, and hold flexible tickets in case your surgeon advises extra recovery nights.
category: Aesthetic, Plastic & Reconstructive Surgery Logistics (ITO Advisory)

body.text: How many days post-op do surgeons typically clear flights for each procedure?

Surgeons generally clear patients to fly after 5 to 7 days for minor procedures such as upper eyelid surgery or gynecomastia, 7 to 10 days for rhinoplasty or breast surgery, and 10 to 14 days for deep-plane facelifts, abdominoplasty, or multi-area body contouring. Per [ISAPS surgery-abroad guidance](https://www.isaps.org/discover/patients-home/considering-your-procedure-abroad/make-a-plan/), patients should remain locally for at least one week.

Flight distance also changes clearance timing. [NHS Royal Orthopaedic Hospital travel guidance](https://roh.nhs.uk/services-information/other-info/before-surgery/travel-surgery-and-dvt) flags flights longer than four hours as higher-risk long-haul travel after general anesthesia. Under [Turkish Airlines medical fitness rules](https://www.turkishairlines.com/uk-int/any-questions/medical-fitness-for-flight-guide-for-illnesses-and-other-medical-conditions/), passengers traveling shortly after recent medical procedures may be asked for a physician's report explicitly stating "medically fit to fly."

body.text: Why do cabin pressure and prolonged sitting raise blood-clot risk?

Prolonged cramped sitting slows venous blood flow in the legs, creating venous stasis, while seat-edge pressure behind the knees can aggravate vessel-wall strain during long flights. Combined with post-surgical inflammation and lower cabin oxygen pressure (hypobaric hypoxia), these factors raise the risk of deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE), per the [CDC Yellow Book](https://www.cdc.gov/yellow-book/hcp/travel-air-sea/deep-vein-thrombosis-and-pulmonary-embolism.html).

[ISAPS post-surgery travel guidance](https://www.isaps.org/discover/patients-home/considering-your-procedure-abroad/post-surgery-considerations-abroad/) warns that post-op patients often struggle to stand or walk the aisle comfortably, compounding clot risk. For higher-risk travelers on flights over six hours, guidelines cited by the CDC recommend aisle seating, regular calf-muscle exercises, periodic walking when safe, hydration, and properly fitted 15–30 mmHg below-the-knee graduated compression stockings if approved by your surgeon.
How do you book airport wheelchair assistance and lounge access at IST?

Book wheelchair assistance directly through your airline at ticket purchase or at least 48 hours before departure. According to [Istanbul Airport Assistance Services](https://www.istairport.com/en/flights/airport-guides/iga-cares-accessibility/accessibility/assistance-service?locale=en), pre-booked passengers receive escorts within 15 minutes via terminal assistance call phones, whereas unreserved arrivals may wait up to 45 minutes.

[Turkish Airlines special assistance](https://www.turkishairlines.com/en-int/any-questions/special-assistance-for-passengers/) provides complimentary wheelchair escorts through security, passport control, and boarding gates for passengers with reduced mobility. Because Istanbul Airport (IST) concourses involve long walking distances, pairing airline wheelchair assistance with [iGA Lounge access](https://www.istairport.com/en/flights/airport-guides/transfer-passenger-guide/services/special-passenger-services/iga-lounge?locale=en) or [iGA Pass Fast Track and Buggy](https://www.istairport.com/en/services/discover/iga-pass-experiences?locale=en) services minimizes standing time and terminal fatigue before boarding.

items: Carry two printed copies and one digital copy of your signed fit-to-fly medical clearance letter.
Confirm your airline wheelchair request code (WCHR or WCHS) appears on your booking confirmation.
Pack all prescribed medications, anticoagulants if prescribed, and discharge notes in carry-on luggage.
Select an aisle seat with extra legroom so you can flex ankles and stand without climbing over others.
Arrange curb-to-door private transfer so you never lift checked suitcases yourself.

body.text: What happens if your surgeon recommends extending your hotel stay?

If your surgeon advises staying extra nights due to lingering swelling, high drain output, or a minor wound concern, delay your flight immediately rather than flying against medical advice. Airlines and travel insurers treat unapproved early departure as a serious safety and coverage liability.

This is why we advise booking flexible or semi-flexible return fares and keeping a 10% to 15% contingency buffer in your travel budget. faq.q: Do airlines at Istanbul Airport always ask to see a fit-to-fly letter?
faq.a: Not every passenger is stopped, but gate agents and cabin crew can deny boarding if visible bandages, facial swelling, or reduced mobility raise safety questions and you lack a signed physician clearance letter.

faq.q: What must a valid fit-to-fly letter include?
faq.a: It should list your full name matching your passport, surgery date, procedure summary, date of final examination, physician's signature and clinic stamp, and an explicit statement that you are medically fit to fly on your scheduled date.

faq.q: Does taking aspirin before my flight prevent post-op blood clots?
faq.a: No. Both CDC-cited chest-physician guidance and NHS travel leaflets note that aspirin is not proven effective for preventing travel-related DVT, and taking unapproved blood thinners after surgery can trigger dangerous bleeding. Only take clot-prevention medication prescribed by your surgeon.

faq.q: Can I carry post-op medical liquids or syringes through IST security?
faq.a: Yes, prescribed medications, saline sprays, and pre-filled anticoagulant syringes are generally permitted in carry-on baggage when accompanied by an English prescription or signed physician letter, though you should declare them at security screening.

faq.q: Is business class required when flying home after plastic surgery?
faq.a: Business class is not mandatory, but lie-flat seating or extra-legroom aisle seats significantly reduce knee flexion and abdominal pressure on flights over four hours. Your surgeon can advise whether seat recline matters for your specific procedure.

faq.q: Can Itinerary of Türkiye issue my fit-to-fly certificate?
faq.a: No. We coordinate your visit. Your licensed medical team makes clinical decisions. Only a licensed physician—typically your operating surgeon—can examine you and issue a valid fit-to-fly medical clearance.
